verdict: Well-sourced and region-focused with a clean bottom line, but fix the greeting placement, explain the half-dozen unfamiliar names, unify the show name and get the founder to sign off the draft view before we record.

First, let's learn how to measure one of these buildings.

worst_three.problem: The listener gets the channel introduction before the first story has delivered a single fact past the hook, so the opening momentum stalls.
worst_three.fix: Move the greeting to after the restaurant gas-line analogy and the first [Pause]. Cut the ident to one line of at most 20 words: 'I'm Wissam, and this is AI Explained.' Use the same show name as the sign-off. That sign-off currently says «AI in the Gulf»; pick one name and drop the « » marks.

worst_three.problem: Listeners hear a run of names they cannot place and lose who is doing what: stc, Brookfield, Ooredoo, Mubbadrah, Rest of World, Climate Central, Mordor Intelligence.
worst_three.fix: Add a few words to each name: 'stc, Saudi Arabia's largest telecom company'; 'Brookfield, the Canadian investment giant'; 'Syntys, a company spun out of Qatar's telecom operator Ooredoo'; 'a consortium led by Mubbadrah, an Omani investment firm'; 'the tech news site Rest of World and the climate research group Climate Central'; 'the market research firm Mordor Intelligence'.

worst_three.problem: About 73 words of dense, alarming facts run straight into a new technical definition with no breath, so the drone strike and the availability-zone idea blur together.
worst_three.fix: Rewrite as: 'Then came a physical attack. In March 2026, AWS said drones had directly struck two of its UAE facilities. A strike near a Bahrain facility also caused damage. Fires set off sprinklers, and the water damaged equipment. [Pause]' Do the same in the Oman–Kuwait passage: add a [Pause] after 'backed by solar and batteries.'
